findings.summary: WorkFolderReconciler.confirm consumes its `files: Iterable[InspectedFile]` argument twice -- once via _plan_entries/sorted and again to build `by_name` -- so a generator-backed source would yield an empty `by_name` and raise a bare KeyError instead of a governed ReconcileError refusal. All current callers pass tuples, so no test exercises it, but the annotation advertises Iterable.

The production entry point `serve()` calls `build_mcp_server(control)` without `work_folders`, so on the live dev-dispatch surface `wf_reconcile` is discoverable but always refuses RECONCILE_SOURCE_UNBOUND; no concrete ReconcileSource exists in the repo outside the test FakeSource. This is disclosed honestly in the findings artifact's 'Remaining hypotheses' section and the spec's boundary excludes deployment work, so it is not scored as a spec violation -- but the human recovery exit is not yet usable end-to-end against a live work folder.

The dispatch context labels 0fb1fe56a7736fef1dc5b15603e1d5e981ff87c5 as the product commit (`work_head_commit`), but the committed implement handoff records `work_head_commit` as 8fc7e3fee1d6fbcc991da3a05a7942b2f1b99a99 with 0fb1fe56 as the stacked metadata-only implementation_subject_commit. The committed handoff is self-consistent with the documented stacking model; the discrepancy is in the dispatch context, not in the product tree.

Scope disclosure: with read-only file inspection only, I could not execute `git diff --exit-code 0fb1fe56 e8705d9a -- . ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'`. I reviewed the product tree as materialized in the worktree and found only the expected reconciliation change plus `.dev-dispatch/` metadata; no evidence of a product file altered by the materialization commit. Actual HEAD verification is left to the deterministic seal.
